evals.prompt: We have a notification service in Go that currently sends messages over email, SMS, and push. We keep having to touch the sending code every time a new channel is added. Sketch a design that lets us add new channels later without rewriting the sender, and show the sending function's signature.
assertions: The channel is selected via a map/dictionary keyed by a string (key -> factory/constructor), NOT via a switch/if-else chain on the channel kind
The map stores factories/constructors that are called only for the selected channel (lazy construction), not pre-built instances of every channel
The core sending function receives the already-resolved channel/port as a parameter (dependency injection), and the registry/map is NOT passed into the sending function

evals.prompt: Our notification core must guarantee that certain sensitive messages only go out over channels that provide end-to-end encryption. We keep adding new channels over time. How should the core enforce this check so it stays correct as channels are added? Show the gating code in Go.
assertions: The gate decides based on a capability/guarantee that the plug-in self-declares as data the core reads, NOT on the plug-in's identity/name (no `if kind == "email"`-style allowlist)
The check is fail-closed / default-deny: a channel is rejected unless the required capability is positively present (a missing or unreadable declaration is treated as a denial)
The rejection error/message names the required capability, never a specific concrete plug-in

evals.prompt: We have a payment-gateway integration that today has a single provider, but we know a second provider is coming and which one to use will be chosen from a config/environment value at deploy time. A colleague proposes selecting the provider with compile-time build tags. Advise us on the selection mechanism and justify it.
assertions: Advises AGAINST compile-time build tags for this case and recommends resolving the provider at load/deploy time via config/DI/registry population (or run-time registry lookup), because the choice comes from a deploy-time config value

Explicitly reasons about binding time — that the moment the variant is chosen determines the technique, and binding compile-time here would force shipping/rebuilding separate binaries to switch a config-selectable provider

evals.prompt: We're building a plug-in registry for export formats in a Go tool. Following the common Go driver idiom (blank import plus an init() that registers the format), a teammate wants each format plug-in to self-register in its own init() at import time. Is that the right approach for our registry? Advise.
assertions: Recommends central/explicit registration at the composition root over init()-based self-registration
Justifies it on the grounds that central wiring is visible/ordered/testable whereas init() self-registration hides the wiring behind import order
